# Vitamins — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/vitamins.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/vitamins.ttl`](../decks/vitamins.ttl) · **Cards:** 35 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The 13 vitamins in 35 cards of three kinds: a vitamin and the chemical name of the vitamin or its main form (e.g. “Vitamin B1: chemical name” → “thiamine”), with separate cards for vitamins D2, D3, K1 and K2; a classic deficiency disease or sign and the vitamin involved (e.g. scurvy → vitamin C); and whether each vitamin is fat-soluble or water-soluble. Text in English and Swedish; no dosage or health advice. Taken from the US National Institutes of Health's Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets and Wikidata, checked against Livsmedelsverket (the Swedish Food Agency) and the Swedish Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The content sources are the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets, which ODS states are in the public domain (and which, as works of the US federal government, are not subject to copyright in the United States), and Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0. The facts on the cards, their selection (the complete set of 13 vitamins, the three card kinds and the seven diseases and signs the ODS sheets tie to one vitamin) and the English and Swedish names all come from these two sources (the Swedish forms A-, C-, D-, E- and K-vitamin included: they are Swedish labels or aliases in Wikidata, which Livsmedelsverket only confirms), so the deck can be CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. No ODS sentence is reproduced in a card: the cards and notes state facts in the compiler's own words, which also respects ODS's request that reproduced content not be altered. Livsmedelsverket (whose material may be reused only on conditions — unedited quotation, attribution and an updating duty — which is not an open licence) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed the facts and the Swedish terms that ODS and Wikidata gave; no wording, table or selection was copied from them, and single-word Swedish technical terms such as "tiamin" or "skörbjugg" are not copyrightable. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the CC0 deck: they remain under their sources' terms (ODS public domain; Livsmedelsverket's text the agency's, quoted verbatim (omissions marked …) and attributed; Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0, by Wikipedia contributors, each linked to the quoted revision) and are short quotations given only to make the verification checkable.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Scope: the 13 vitamins of human nutrition, the complete set, for each of which the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements (ODS) publishes one health-professional fact sheet (A, D, E and K fat-soluble; thiamin, riboflavin, niacin, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6, biotin, folate, vitamin B12 and C water-soluble). The Swedish Food Agency's index page confirms the same 13 ("Det finns 13 livsnödvändiga vitaminer"). The set of 13 is the complete set, not a selection taken from a list.
3. ODS fact sheets: ods.od.nih.gov answered every request from the research environment (curl and WebFetch) with a Cloudflare challenge page or HTTP 403 (query 6), and its API did the same (query 7). The 13 health-professional fact sheets were therefore downloaded unmodified from the Internet Archive's most recent 2026 capture of each (query 8: a request for https://web.archive.org/web/2026id_/<page> redirects to the latest 2026 capture; captures 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-04, all of the current versions, which were last updated between 2021 and 2026), decompressed and turned into plain text (totext.py), and the relevant sentences were extracted with grep_ods.py (queries 9–13). Every ODS quotation in the evidence is verbatim from these captures; each locator names the sheet, its "Updated" date and the capture.
4. Wikidata: query 1 asked for items that are instances or subclasses of vitamin (Q34956); it returned only classes (fat-soluble vitamin Q4389811, water-soluble vitamin Q11548920, vitamin B Q183206 …), not the 13 vitamins. Query 2 found the items labelled or aliased "vitamin A" … "vitamin K2" in English; query 3 (wbsearchentities, search.py) found the items for the diseases and the vitamers. Query 4 (entities.py, wbgetentities) fetched the English and Swedish labels and aliases, the Wikipedia sitelinks and the statements P31, P279, P828, P2176, P361 and P527 of 41 candidate items; query 5 resolved the deficiency items the diseases point to; query 14 found which Swedish terms are labels or aliases of which items; query 15 listed the members of the fat- and water-soluble classes; query 16 fetched the folates item Q111271197. All raw responses were saved.
5. Card kind 1, vitamin → chemical name: for each vitamin the ODS sheet gives either one compound (thiamin(e), riboflavin, pantothenic acid, biotin, L-ascorbic acid) or a generic name for several vitamers (niacin for nicotinic acid and nicotinamide; folate, including folic acid; cobalamins). For vitamins A, B6 and E, which are groups with no single chemical name, the front names the form asked for in a front note: the main form of vitamin A, an alcohol (retinol, ODS: "primarily retinol and retinyl esters"); the alcohol among the B6 vitamers (pyridoxine, ODS: "pyridoxine, an alcohol; pyridoxal, an aldehyde; and pyridoxamine"); and the form of vitamin E that meets human requirements (alpha-tocopherol, ODS). Vitamins D and K have no generic card: vitamin K has no chemical name of its own (ODS: "the generic name for a family of compounds"), and "calciferol", which ODS gives as another name for vitamin D, is also a name of ergocalciferol alone (it is an English alias of Q139200, ergocalciferol), so it would not have one right answer; instead their two main forms each have a card (D2 ergocalciferol, D3 cholecalciferol; K1 phylloquinone, K2 menaquinones), all named in the ODS sheets.
6. Card kind 2, deficiency disease or sign → vitamin: only diseases and signs that an ODS sheet itself ties to one vitamin. Five are diseases caused by the lack of the vitamin: scurvy (vitamin C), rickets and osteomalacia (vitamin D), beriberi (thiamin) and pellagra (niacin). Night blindness is not a disease but an early sign of vitamin A deficiency ("The first sign" of xerophthalmia, "the most common clinical sign of vitamin A deficiency"), and its card asks for it as such. Pernicious anemia goes the other way: it is an autoimmune disease that causes vitamin B12 deficiency (ODS: "the most common cause of clinically evident vitamin B12 deficiency"; it leads to "malabsorption of dietary vitamin B12"), not a disease caused by it, and its card asks which vitamin it leaves the body short of. Each was confirmed by Livsmedelsverket's page on the vitamin and by the Swedish Wikipedia article on the disease, and, where Wikidata has the link, by the disease item (scurvy P828 ascorbic acid deficiency; beriberi P279 thiamine deficiency; pellagra P828 niacin deficiency; pernicious anemia P828 vitamin B12 deficiency).
7. Card kind 3, fat- or water-soluble: the introduction of each ODS sheet states it ("fat-soluble" for A, D, E and K; "water-soluble" for the other nine; for pantothenic acid and biotin in the sentence after the introduction's first, "this water-soluble B vitamin", "This water-soluble vitamin"). Livsmedelsverket's index page gives the same split. Wikidata states it for A, D, E and K (P279 fat-soluble vitamin Q4389811) and for biotin, folate (vitamin B9) and vitamin B12 through their class vitamin B (P279 Q183206, itself P279 water-soluble vitamin Q11548920); those statements are machine-checked.
8. Swedish text: the Swedish names of the compounds and diseases are Wikidata Swedish labels or aliases where Wikidata has them (tiamin, pantotensyra, pyridoxin, niacin, askorbinsyra, kolekalciferol, folat, skörbjugg, rakit, beriberi, pellagra, perniciös anemi, nattblindhet; Riboflavin, Biotin, Kobalamin, Retinol, Fyllokinon, Menakinon and Osteomalaci are capitalised in Wikidata and written in lower case on the cards, as Swedish common nouns are). Every Swedish name on a card side was then confirmed in Livsmedelsverket's page on the vitamin (queries 17–19) and in the introduction of the Swedish Wikipedia article (query 20, with revision ids); the term "xeroftalmi", which appears only in the night-blindness note, is the Wikidata Swedish label of Q1054713 and is confirmed by the Swedish Wikipedia article Xeroftalmi (Livsmedelsverket does not use it). The Swedish forms of the vitamin names are Wikidata Swedish labels or aliases (C-vitamin on Q199678, D-vitamin on Q175621, K-vitamin on Q182338, A-vitamin on retinol Q424976, E-vitamin and Alfa-tokoferol on tocopherol Q910277; Vitamin B1 … Vitamin B12 as aliases of the B-vitamin items), and Livsmedelsverket confirms them as the forms Swedish authorities use: A-, C-, D-, E- and K-vitamin, but vitamin B1 … vitamin B12 and vitamin D2, D3, K1, K2. Swedish "vitamin" is neuter, so the solubility answers are "fettlösligt" and "vattenlösligt". Svenska Akademiens ordböcker (svenska.se) could not be used as a check: the lookup pages now render in the browser and returned no entries to a script (svenska_se.py, which fetched https://svenska.se/tri/f_so.php?sok=<word> and https://svenska.se/tri/f_saol.php?sok=<word> for tiamin, riboflavin, niacin, pantotensyra, pyridoxin, biotin, folat, kobalamin, askorbinsyra, kalciferol, tokoferol, retinol, skörbjugg, rakit, beriberi, pellagra, osteomalaci, nattblindhet, perniciös, fettlöslig and vattenlöslig; svenska.se is not a source of the deck). Two web searches for a Swedish source for the generic name "kalciferol" (WebSearch: "kalciferol" D-vitamin; WebSearch: kalciferol vitamin D ne.se OR 1177.se OR fass.se OR internetmedicin.se) found none, only German pharmacy pages and FASS product texts about cholecalciferol, another reason the generic vitamin D card was left out.
9. Notes: a back note, in the compiler's own words, gives the other vitamers or a short piece of context where it helps (e.g. folic acid as the synthetic form of folate, the cobalt in cobalamin, osteomalacia as the adult counterpart of rickets). Every fact in a note is stated in an ODS sheet or Wikidata and was checked against Livsmedelsverket or the Swedish Wikipedia; no dosages, intake recommendations or health advice are given.
10. Licences: the ODS site-policy page (query 21, archived capture), Livsmedelsverket's reuse page (query 22), Wikidata:Licensing (query 23) and a Swedish Wikipedia footer (query 24) were fetched and quoted in the sources.
11. Helper scripts (Python 3, standard library; kept in the authoring session's scratch directory, so their logic is given here): fetch_ods_wayback.py requests https://web.archive.org/web/2026id_/<page> for each ODS page (the id_ form returns the archived bytes unmodified), follows the redirect to the latest 2026 capture, records the capture timestamp and saves the HTML; totext.py gunzips an archived page when needed, drops <script> and <style>, turns </p>, </li>, </h1>–</h6>, </tr>, </div> and <br> into line breaks, removes the remaining tags, unescapes HTML entities and collapses white space; grep_ods.py splits each sheet's plain text into sentences (at ".", "!" or "?" followed by white space and a capital letter) and prints the sentences matching a case-insensitive regular expression, for all 13 sheets or the ones named; entities.py calls wbgetentities (query 4) in batches and prints the labels, aliases, sitelinks and the listed statements of each item; search.py calls wbsearchentities (query 3) for each term; svwiki.py calls the Swedish Wikipedia API of query 20 and prints each article's title, revision id and introduction; fetch_lv.sh is the curl loop of query 17; lv_main.py keeps the text of each Livsmedelsverket page from its <h1> to </main>, with the same tag stripping as totext.py.
12. Build: the dossier was written by hand, built with python3 scripts/authored_decks.py build vitamins (which runs every card's Wikidata checks against live Wikidata) and validated with node scripts/validate_sources.ts vitamins.

## Selection

All 13 vitamins of human nutrition (the complete set, one ODS fact sheet each; Livsmedelsverket confirms the same 13), in three kinds of card. Chemical names: one card for each vitamin whose ODS sheet gives a single compound or a generic name (B1, B2, B3, B5, B7, B9, B12, C), one for each of A, B6 and E naming one form identified by a front note, and one each for vitamins D2, D3, K1 and K2 instead of a generic card for D and K (15 cards). Left out: a generic card for vitamin D ("calciferol" also names ergocalciferol alone, so the card would have two readings) and for vitamin K (no chemical name of its own); provitamin A carotenoids and the metabolites calcidiol and calcitriol; vitamin K3 (menadione, synthetic). Deficiency diseases and signs: the seven whose link to one vitamin the ODS sheets state and the other sources confirm: the deficiency diseases scurvy, rickets, osteomalacia, beriberi and pellagra; night blindness, an early sign of vitamin A deficiency rather than a disease; and pernicious anemia, an autoimmune disease that causes vitamin B12 deficiency rather than one caused by it (7 cards). Left out: megaloblastic anemia (caused by lack of either folate or vitamin B12, so it has two answers), xerophthalmia (kept in the night-blindness note: night blindness is the better-known first sign), Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome (also thiamine deficiency, mentioned in the beriberi note), vitamin K deficiency bleeding and ariboflavinosis (their names give the answer away), neural tube defects (a risk associated with low folate, not a deficiency disease) and conditions without a classic single-vitamin cause. Solubility: one card per vitamin (13 cards). No card gives a dose, an intake recommendation, a food source or health advice.

## Queries

**1. Items that are instances or subclasses of vitamin (Q34956) (returned only classes)** (Wikidata: the items on the vitamins and their vitamers (e.g. Q83187 thiamine, Q424976 retinol, Q139347 cholecalciferol, Q186093 phylloquinone), the classes fat-soluble vitamin (Q4389811) and vitamin B (Q183206), and the deficiency diseases (e.g. Q163865 scurvy, Q184084 beriberi), with their English and Swedish labels and aliases)

```
SELECT ?item ?rel ?en ?sv WHERE {
  VALUES ?rel { wdt:P31 wdt:P279 }
  ?item ?rel wd:Q34956 .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?en
```

**2. Items whose English label or alias is "vitamin A" … "vitamin K2", with their classes** (Wikidata: the items on the vitamins and their vitamers (e.g. Q83187 thiamine, Q424976 retinol, Q139347 cholecalciferol, Q186093 phylloquinone), the classes fat-soluble vitamin (Q4389811) and vitamin B (Q183206), and the deficiency diseases (e.g. Q163865 scurvy, Q184084 beriberi), with their English and Swedish labels and aliases)

```
SELECT ?name ?item ?kind ?en ?sv ?class ?classEn WHERE {
  VALUES ?name { "vitamin A"@en "vitamin B1"@en "vitamin B2"@en "vitamin B3"@en "vitamin B5"@en "vitamin B6"@en "vitamin B7"@en "vitamin B9"@en "vitamin B12"@en "vitamin C"@en "vitamin D"@en "vitamin E"@en "vitamin K"@en "vitamin D2"@en "vitamin D3"@en "vitamin K1"@en "vitamin K2"@en }
  { ?item rdfs:label ?name BIND("label" AS ?kind) } UNION { ?item skos:altLabel ?name BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { { ?item wdt:P31 ?class } UNION { ?item wdt:P279 ?class }
    ?class rdfs:label ?classEn FILTER(LANG(?classEn) = "en") }
}
ORDER BY ?name ?item
```

**3. Search for the disease and vitamer items (search.py: wbsearchentities, English, top 4 hits per term)** (Wikidata: the items on the vitamins and their vitamers (e.g. Q83187 thiamine, Q424976 retinol, Q139347 cholecalciferol, Q186093 phylloquinone), the classes fat-soluble vitamin (Q4389811) and vitamin B (Q183206), and the deficiency diseases (e.g. Q163865 scurvy, Q184084 beriberi), with their English and Swedish labels and aliases)

```
python3 search.py beriberi pellagra xerophthalmia osteomalacia "pernicious anemia" "night blindness" "Wernicke encephalopathy" "folate" "folic acid" "nicotinic acid" "tocopherol" "phylloquinone" "calciferol" "thiamine" "cobalamin" "ascorbic acid" "retinol" "alpha-tocopherol"
# each term: https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&search=<term>&language=en&limit=4&format=json
```

**4. Labels, aliases (en, sv, mul), en/sv sitelinks and statements P31, P279, P828, P1542, P2176, P361, P527, P1990, P921 of the candidate items (entities.py)** (Wikidata: the items on the vitamins and their vitamers (e.g. Q83187 thiamine, Q424976 retinol, Q139347 cholecalciferol, Q186093 phylloquinone), the classes fat-soluble vitamin (Q4389811) and vitamin B (Q183206), and the deficiency diseases (e.g. Q163865 scurvy, Q184084 beriberi), with their English and Swedish labels and aliases)

```
https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities&ids=<up to 40 ids>&props=labels|aliases|claims|sitelinks&languages=en|sv|mul&sitefilter=enwiki|svwiki&format=json
# ids: Q18225 Q424976 Q83187 Q46222910 Q130365 Q30715691 Q134658 Q192423 Q179894 Q205130 Q423746 Q181354 Q92079055 Q127060 Q187706 Q71272629 Q3329800 Q199678 Q193598 Q175621 Q139347 Q139200 Q141180 Q910277 Q158348 Q182338 Q186093 Q7936967 Q4389811 Q6164057 Q11548920 Q163865 Q183392 Q184084 Q221441 Q1054713 Q860395 Q1346016 Q7758678 Q1573307 Q34956
```

**5. The deficiency items the disease items point to, with their classes and causes** (Wikidata: the items on the vitamins and their vitamers (e.g. Q83187 thiamine, Q424976 retinol, Q139347 cholecalciferol, Q186093 phylloquinone), the classes fat-soluble vitamin (Q4389811) and vitamin B (Q183206), and the deficiency diseases (e.g. Q163865 scurvy, Q184084 beriberi), with their English and Swedish labels and aliases)

SELECT ?item ?en ?sv ?p ?v ?vEn WHERE {

**6. Direct download of the fact sheets (every response was a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." challenge page; WebFetch got HTTP 403)** (Office of Dietary Supplements: Vitamin and Mineral Supplement Fact Sheets (health-professional fact sheets on vitamin A, thiamin, riboflavin, niacin, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6, biotin, folate, vitamin B12, vitamin C, vitamin D, vitamin E and vitamin K))

```
for s in VitaminA Thiamin Riboflavin Niacin PantothenicAcid VitaminB6 Biotin Folate VitaminB12 VitaminC VitaminD VitaminE VitaminK; do curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o "$OUT/$s.html" "https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/$s-HealthProfessional/"; done
```

**7. ## Quality control

6 rounds, 32 findings: 27 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 5 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (99 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card against the ODS fact sheet for the vitamin, Wikidata where it has the statement or label, Livsmedelsverket's page on the vitamin and the Swedish Wikipedia article; the Swedish names; card ambiguity. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 35 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

ODS, Livsmedelsverket and the Swedish Wikipedia agree on every card. Wikidata agrees wherever it has the fact, but its vitamin items are unevenly modelled: several labels are capitalised or name a related item, one Swedish label is wrong (ergocalciferol), and solubility is stated only for A, D, E, K and the B-group class. No card follows a Wikidata value that a better source contradicts; where Wikidata's form differs from the card (case, singular/plural, a related item), the check verifies the Wikidata form and the evidence says so, and no check was skipped to hide a disagreement. The builder's checks cover the names on 15 chemical-name cards, the disease names and four disease-to-deficiency links, and solubility for seven vitamins. The brief's generic vitamin D card (calciferol) was not made, because the name is ambiguous.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| (deck) | The brief asked for a card "vitamin D → calciferol (D2 ergocalciferol, D3 cholecalciferol)". ODS writes "Vitamin D (also referred to as calciferol)", but "calciferol" is also a name of ergocalciferol (vitamin D2) alone: it is an English alias of Wikidata's ergocalciferol item (Q139200) as well as of vitamin D (Q175621). No Swedish source for a generic "kalciferol" was found (Livsmedelsverket and the Swedish Wikipedia use only kolekalciferol and ergokalciferol; the Swedish alias "Kalciferol" is on Q175621 only). | No generic vitamin D card; one card each for vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol) and vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol), which ODS and Livsmedelsverket both name as the two main forms. Vitamin K likewise gets K1 and K2 cards and no generic card, since ODS calls vitamin K "the generic name for a family of compounds". | fixed |
| vitamin-d2-name | Wikidata's Swedish label of ergocalciferol (Q139200) is "Cladonia arbuscula", the name of a lichen: a wrong label. | The Swedish back "ergokalciferol" is checked against the Swedish alias "Ergokalciferol" of vitamin D (Q175621), whose P527 (has part) is Q139200, and confirmed by Livsmedelsverket ("vitamin D2 (ergokalciferol)") and the Swedish Wikipedia. The wrong label was not used and not edited. | fixed |
| vitamin-e-name | Vitamin E is eight compounds (four tocopherols, four tocotrienols); "tocopherol" alone would not name one form. Wikidata's tocopherol class (Q910277) has the Swedish label "Alfatokoferol" (the name of one member) and alias "Alfa-tokoferol"; RRR-alpha-tocopherol (Q158348) has no English label or alias spelt "alpha-tocopherol" (only "Alpha Tocopherol", "d-alpha-tocopherol" and similar). | The front note asks for the form that meets human requirements, which ODS names ("Alpha- (or α-) tocopherol is the only form that is recognized to meet human requirements") and Livsmedelsverket confirms (alfa-tokoferol, "den form av E-vitamin som är nödvändig för kroppens funktioner"). Back "alpha-tocopherol" (ODS spelling) / "alfa-tokoferol" (Livsmedelsverket's spelling). Checks: Q910277 Swedish alias "Alfa-tokoferol" and Q910277 P279 vitamin E (Q141180); the English form rests on ODS and the Swedish Wikipedia. | fixed |
| vitamin-a-name | Vitamin A is a group (ODS: "primarily retinol and retinyl esters"; retinal and retinoic acid are its active metabolites), so "chemical name" alone has several answers. | Front note "its main form, an alcohol": retinol is the alcohol ("-ol") and the form the others are converted to (ODS: "Retinyl esters and provitamin A carotenoids are converted to retinol"). Wikidata: retinol (Q424976) P279 vitamin A (Q18225), English alias "Vitamin A1". The same device is used for vitamin B6 (front note "the alcohol among its forms": pyridoxine, ODS "pyridoxine, an alcohol; pyridoxal, an aldehyde; and pyridoxamine"). | fixed |
| pernicious-anemia | Pernicious anemia is an autoimmune disease of the stomach that causes vitamin B12 deficiency (ODS); it is not caused by a lack of B12 in the diet. Wikidata models it as having cause (P828) vitamin B12 deficiency, and the Swedish Wikipedia calls it anemia arising from B12 deficiency. | The front asks which vitamin pernicious anemia leaves the body short of ("leads to a deficiency of which vitamin?" / "ger brist på vilket vitamin?"), true on both readings; the note says it is autoimmune and stops B12 being absorbed (ODS; Livsmedelsverket: "en autoimmun sjukdom som innebär att patienten har svårt att ta upp vitamin B12"). The P828 check is kept because the fact it checks, the link to B12 deficiency, is right. | fixed |
| night-blindness | The brief's deficiency list suggested classic links only; night blindness also has non-nutritional causes (e.g. retinitis pigmentosa, as the Swedish Wikipedia notes), and the ODS term for the vitamin A deficiency disease is xerophthalmia, whose first sign is night blindness. | Front "Night blindness: an early sign of a deficiency of which vitamin?", which has one answer; the note names xerophthalmia. Livsmedelsverket ("Lindrig brist kan ge nattblindhet") and the Swedish Wikipedia ("Den vanligaste orsaken till nattblindhet är a-vitaminbrist") confirm. | fixed |
| rickets | Rickets and osteomalacia are classically vitamin D deficiency, but rare forms have other causes (e.g. inherited disorders of vitamin D metabolism, phosphate loss). | Both cards ask for the vitamin whose deficiency causes them, as ODS states ("Vitamin D deficiency can manifest as rickets in children and as osteomalacia in adolescents and adults"); the notes link the two (children/adults). The other causes are not covered by a card. | no change needed |
| (deck) | Wikidata writes several Swedish labels with a capital (Riboflavin, Biotin, Kobalamin, Retinol, Fyllokinon, Menakinon, Osteomalaci) and some items under a singular or related name (menaquinone, not menaquinones; phylloquinone only as the alias "Phylloquinone"; vitamin B12's Swedish label is "Kobalamin"; vitamin B9 has no Swedish label, and "folat" is the label of Q111271197 "folates", a subclass of folic acid). | Cards use lower case for Swedish common nouns and the plural "menaquinones"/"menakinoner" as ODS and Livsmedelsverket do; each check verifies the form Wikidata has and the card's evidence states the difference. Livsmedelsverket and the Swedish Wikipedia confirm every Swedish form on the cards. | no change needed |
| (deck) | Wikidata states water-solubility only through the class vitamin B (Q183206, subclass of water-soluble vitamin Q11548920), and only biotin, vitamin B9 and vitamin B12 are subclasses of vitamin B; thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6 and vitamin C have no solubility statement. | Solubility rests on each ODS sheet's introduction and Livsmedelsverket's index page for all 13 cards; the Wikidata statements that exist (A, D, E, K fat-soluble; biotin, B9, B12 through vitamin B) are machine-checked. | no change needed |
| (deck) | ods.od.nih.gov refused every request from the research environment (Cloudflare challenge, HTTP 403), including its API. | The 13 fact sheets and the Site Policies page were read in the Internet Archive's most recent 2026 captures (2026-08-13 for the policy page, 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-04 for the sheets); each evidence locator gives the capture. The sheets' "Updated" dates (2021–2026) predate the captures, so the captures show the current versions. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 35 cards against standard nutrition facts, spot checks of the ODS captures, a live run of the builder's Wikidata checks (97 checks) and the disease items on Wikidata.

No factual error on any card. One warning: the deck's description, selection and method called all seven kind-2 cards diseases caused by a lack of the vitamin, which fits neither night blindness (a sign) nor pernicious anemia (a disease that causes B12 deficiency). Three suggestions on check strength and one note's wording. All four were verified and applied.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| (deck) | The description, selection and method step on kind-2 cards said every card is a deficiency disease caused by a lack of the vitamin; night blindness is a sign of vitamin A deficiency, and pernicious anemia is an autoimmune disease that causes vitamin B12 deficiency, which the method's own ODS quotation says. | Verified against the ODS vitamin A and B12 captures. Description reworded to "a classic deficiency disease or sign and the vitamin involved" / "en klassisk bristsjukdom eller ett bristtecken och vilket vitamin det gäller"; the method step and the selection now say that five are deficiency diseases, night blindness is an early sign and pernicious anemia causes B12 deficiency; the licensing paragraph says "diseases and signs". The cards were already worded correctly and are unchanged. | fixed |
| vitamin-e-name | Both Wikidata checks ran against the tocopherol class Q910277, not against the compound that is the answer. | Confirmed today with wbgetentities: Q158348 RRR-alpha-tocopherol has P279 Q910277. Added the check Q158348 P279 Q910277 and recorded the item's labels in the evidence. Wikidata still has no English label spelt "alpha-tocopherol", so the English form rests on ODS. | fixed |
| vitamin-b1-solubility | The card's only Wikidata check was the label "vitamin B1", which says nothing about solubility. | Check removed (the label is still checked on vitamin-b1-name); the card now has no checks, like B2, B3, B5, B6 and C, and its evidence says why. The extra label checks on vitamin-d-solubility and vitamin-e-solubility are kept: those cards also have the P279 fat-soluble check, and the label checks verify the front's wording. | fixed |
| vitamin-k2-name | The note "designated MK-4 to MK-13" may be read as the complete range, and "mostly of bacterial origin" as covering MK-4. | Note softened to "Mostly made by bacteria; named MK-n (e.g. MK-4, MK-7) after the length of their side chain." / "Bildas främst av bakterier; betecknas MK-n (t.ex. MK-4, MK-7) efter sidokedjans längd."; the ODS sentence naming MK-4, MK-7 and MK-9 as the best-studied menaquinones was added to the evidence. | fixed |

### Round 2: Language, translation and language tags (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent language, translation and language tags reviewer · **Scope:** All 35 cards, the title, description and keywords in English and Swedish, and the language tags.

No errors or warnings: every card text is tagged en or sv and the Swedish terms are the established forms. Six suggestions on consistency and idiom; five applied, one (untagged keywords) is a builder limitation outside this dossier.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| vitamin-e-name | The Swedish front note "den form som kroppen behöver" is looser than the English "the form that meets human requirements" and could suggest the other forms are useless. | Changed to "den form som täcker människans behov", which follows ODS ("the only form that is recognized to meet human requirements"). | fixed |
| beriberi | The English note writes Wernicke–Korsakoff with an en dash, the Swedish one with a hyphen. | The Swedish note now uses the en dash too: "Wernicke–Korsakoffs syndrom", the dash used between two personal names in such a compound. | fixed |
| vitamin-b1-name | British "spelt" mixed with American "anemia" (which follows ODS). | Changed to "Also spelled thiamin", following ODS's American English throughout. | fixed |
| vitamin-b6-name | "Vitamin B6 is six compounds" (and "Vitamin E is eight compounds" on vitamin-e-name) is unidiomatic English. | Changed to "comprises six compounds" and "comprises eight compounds" (vitamin-e-name changed too). | fixed |
| (deck) | The English description uses straight ASCII quotation marks, the Swedish one typographic ones. | The English description now uses “…”. | fixed |
| (deck) | The keywords are emitted as untagged literals because the builder takes them as a plain list of strings. | Confirmed in the builder (docstring: "keywords list of strings"). The dossier cannot tag them; this is for the library maintainer to change in the builder, which this deck's author does not edit. | no change needed |

### Round 3: Licensing, attribution and documentation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer · **Scope:** All 35 cards' evidence (every non-Wikidata locator refetched and compared), the four sources' licence pages, the licensing, method and queries.

No licence breach; every recorded licence is right and a CC0 deck is compliant. Four warnings (two unsourced qualifiers in notes, a self-contradiction on where the Swedish vitamin-name forms come from, and Swedish notes worded close to Livsmedelsverket) and five suggestions; all verified and applied.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |

The card's Swedish Wikipedia evidence now says that the article equates the two, that it confirms only the Swedish name, and that the notes follow ODS and Livsmedelsverket. | night-blindness | The Swedish term "xeroftalmi" in the back note rested only on Wikidata's sv label (Q1054713); Livsmedelsverket does not use it and the quoted Nattblindhet introduction does not contain it, although the method said every Swedish name was confirmed in both. | Verified: the Swedish Wikipedia article Xeroftalmi exists (revision 54264507) and its introduction reads "Xeroftalmi är en ögonsjukdom som uppstår då ögats slemhinnor uttorkas (till exempel i brist på vitamin A retinol)." Added as evidence on the card; the wikipedia-sv source title and query 20 now include the article, and the method's Swedish-text step says that note-only "xeroftalmi" rests on the Wikidata label and the Swedish Wikipedia, not Livsmedelsverket. | fixed |
